items.title: House panel advances bill cutting US UN funding by 78%

featured_image.name: Trump's FY2027 Budget Is Not Just a Spending Plan - ONEST Network

items.description:
The House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs advanced a fiscal year 2027 spending bill on Wednesday that would dramatically reduce US funding for international organizations, slashing contributions by roughly 78% and effectively zeroing out US dues for the UN regular budget.

The bill, released on April 22 and marked up on April 23, allocates $310.2 million for Contributions to International Organizations — down from $1.39 billion enacted in fiscal year 2026. It provides $489.5 million for UN peacekeeping activities, a roughly 60% reduction from the $1.23 billion provided in the current fiscal year. The legislation eliminates the International Organizations and Programs account entirely, cutting all voluntary US contributions to agencies including UNICEF, the UN Development Programme, and UN Women.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump threatens UK with tariffs over digital services tax

featured_image.name: Trump warns of 'big tariff' if UK does not drop digital services ...

items.description: President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that the United States could impose a "big tariff" on the United Kingdom if it does not eliminate its digital services tax on American tech companies, escalating a long-running dispute over levies that Washington considers discriminatory against US firms.

items.title: INNIO completes first 3 MW hydrogen backup test for data centers

featured_image.name: Hydrogen moves INNIO's Jenbacher site closer to climate neutrality ...

items.description: INNIO Group and the Net Zero Innovation Hub for Data Centers have completed what they describe as the world's first demonstration of 100% hydrogen-fueled backup power at the 3 MW scale, a milestone aimed at replacing diesel generators in mission-critical data center operations. The test, announced on Wednesday, was witnessed by technical experts from Microsoft, Google, and Data4.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended three weeks

featured_image.name: Trump's Lebanon ceasefire takes Israel by surprise

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has been extended by three weeks, according to a post on Truth Social, just days before the truce was set to expire on April 26. The extension came as Israeli and Lebanese diplomats held a second round of rare direct talks in Washington.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Nuclear power surges worldwide as Chernobyl's 40th anniversary approaches

featured_image.name: 2026 China International Nuclear Industry Exhibition

items.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, nuclear energy is experiencing a resurgence that would have seemed unthinkable in the decades following the catastrophic 1986 explosion. More than 400 nuclear reactors now operate across 31 countries, with roughly 70 more under construction, and a growing coalition of nations has pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050.[1][2]

items.title: Meta to cut 8,000 jobs starting May 20, more layoffs planned for 2026

featured_image.name: Meta lays off employees working on VR in Reality Labs division

items.description:
Meta is preparing to lay off approximately 10% of its global workforce — close to 8,000 employees — beginning May 20, according to Reuters, in what the company views as the first wave of broader cuts planned throughout 2026.[1][2]

Three sources familiar with the plans told Reuters that additional layoffs are expected in the second half of the year, though the timing and scope of those subsequent rounds have not been finalized. The pace of future cuts may depend in part on how the company's artificial intelligence capabilities evolve, the sources said.[3][4][5][2]

items.title: Microsoft offers first voluntary buyout in its 51-year history

featured_image.name: Microsoft is requiring employees return to the office - Yahoo Finance

items.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary retirement buyout packages to a portion of its U.S. workforce, marking the first such program in the company's 51-year history. The one-time initiative, disclosed in an internal memo on Thursday, represents a new approach for the tech giant as it continues reshaping its workforce amid a sweeping industry pivot toward artificial intelligence.

items.title: U.S. seizes another Iranian tanker as Hormuz crisis deepens

featured_image.name: US seizes another tanker carrying Iranian oil in Indian Ocean

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps seized two container ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, marking the first confirmed vessel seizures since the U.S.-Iran war began in late February and further choking off one of the world's most critical trade routes.

items.title: 40,000 Samsung workers stage largest protest, threaten strike

featured_image.name: Samsung Electronics workers rally for bonus system overhaul ...

items.description: Tens of thousands of Samsung Electronics workers rallied on Thursday at the company's semiconductor complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, demanding higher bonuses and threatening an extended strike that could disrupt global AI chip supplies.

items.title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS traced to cold, ancient corner of the Milky Way

featured_image.name: Interstellar object Comet 3I/ATLAS leaving the solar system

items.description:
A comet that streaked through our solar system from another star likely originated in a frigid, remote region of the galaxy that had yet to form its own planetary system, astronomers announced on Thursday.

Comet 3I/ATLAS, only the third confirmed interstellar visitor and quite possibly the oldest, may be up to 11 billion years old — more than twice the age of our sun, according to the study published in Nature Astronomy.[1][2]

items.title: France probes weather sensor tampering tied to Polymarket bets

featured_image.name: Le siège de Météo France transformé en église russe

items.description: French authorities have opened a criminal investigation into the suspected physical manipulation of a weather sensor at Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport after two brief, unexplained temperature spikes this month lined up with winning bets on the cryptocurrency prediction platform Polymarket, netting at least one trader roughly $34,000.

items.title: China warns of 'critical juncture' as Iran ceasefire talks falter

featured_image.name: Will China join Pakistan-led efforts to mediate US-Iran peace?

items.description: As the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran approaches its third month with a fragile ceasefire hanging in the balance, China has quietly positioned itself as one of the most active diplomatic players working to prevent a return to full-scale hostilities. Beijing's behind-the-scenes efforts — ranging from dozens of high-level phone calls to joint proposals with Pakistan — underscore a broader ambition to reshape its role in Middle Eastern affairs.

items.title: EU formally approves €90B Ukraine loan, new Russia sanctions

featured_image.name: EU gives final approval to €90-billion loan for Ukraine

items.description: European Union leaders convened in the Cypriot resort town of Agia Napa on Thursday for a two-day informal summit dominated by the energy crisis triggered by the Strait of Hormuz blockade, the war in Ukraine, and escalating tensions in the Middle East.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says 'no time frame' on Iran war as prices soar

featured_image.name: US says no time frame for ending war, as Iran says reopening ...

items.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched airstrikes on Iran on February 28, the economic aftershocks of the conflict continue to ripple across global markets, pushing oil prices to levels not seen in years, raising grocery bills from Washington to Sydney, and sparking a worldwide revival in biofuel investment.

items.title: U.S.-Iran peace talks stall as Hormuz standoff pushes oil past $100

featured_image.name: Oil prices rise as US extends ceasefire, puts peace talks on hold

items.description:
Crude oil prices climbed sharply this week, with Brent crude breaking back above $100 per barrel on Wednesday, as an extended but fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran failed to ease a mounting maritime standoff in the Strait of Hormuz that continues to choke global energy supplies.

Brent crude rose approximately 3.5 percent on Wednesday to $101.91 per barrel, according to The New York Times, while West Texas Intermediate crude edged up to $92.96. The gains followed a volatile stretch that saw prices jump roughly 5 percent on Tuesday amid uncertainty over the ceasefire's expiration, according to The National.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says China helped push Iran toward ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes China got Iran to negotiate, AFP reports ...

items.description:
As the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran grinds through its second month, China has quietly positioned itself as a pivotal diplomatic player, leveraging its economic ties with Tehran and its desire for global leadership to carve out an outsized role in mediation efforts.

Chinese President Xi Jinping this week called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz during a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Monday, reaffirming Beijing's commitment to "all efforts conducive to restoring peace". The intervention followed weeks of intensive behind-the-scenes diplomacy. China's top diplomat Wang Yi made 26 phone calls between the start of the conflict on February 28 and the lead-up to the April 8 ceasefire, according to Al Jazeera.[1][2]

items.title: Tesla raises capex plan to $25 billion for AI push

featured_image.name: Elon Musk's plan to redesign the world's factories... and perhaps the  planet too: humanoid robots that work 12 hours a day, never rest, and use  artificial intelligence

items.description: Tesla will spend more than $25 billion on capital expenditures this year, roughly tripling last year's outlay, as the electric vehicle maker accelerates its pivot towards artificial intelligence and robotics amid a slowing car business.

items.title: Nuclear leaders convene in Busan, framing reactors as AI-era infrastructure

featured_image.name: Nuclear Leaders Highlight Power Needs for AI Era

items.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, the nuclear power industry finds itself in the midst of a striking resurgence. Driven by surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence, climate targets, and fresh government commitments, roughly 75 reactors are now under construction worldwide and about 120 more are planned, according to the World Nuclear Association.[1][2]

items.title: Asian shares retreat from record highs as oil tops $103 on Iran tensions

featured_image.name: Asian stock markets plunge amid Trump's ultimatum on Iran

items.description: Asian markets pulled back on Thursday after briefly touching record highs, as rising oil prices and uncertainty over the U.S.-Iran conflict prompted investors to lock in profits from a weeks-long technology-driven rally.

items.title: IDF removes 40 Israeli settlers who crossed into Syria

featured_image.name: Israeli troops remove Israeli settler group who crossed into ...

items.description:
Around 40 Israeli settler activists from the far-right Pioneers of Bashan organization crossed into Syrian territory on Wednesday, barricading themselves on a rooftop on the outskirts of the Druze village of Hader at the foot of Mount Hermon and demanding the Israeli government approve Jewish settlements in Syria.[1][2][3]

The Israeli military said the group gathered near the northern border before advancing several hundred meters — roughly half a kilometer — into Syria. IDF troops escorted the activists back to Israeli territory and handed them over to police.[2][1]

"The IDF strongly condemns this incident and emphasizes its severity, which constitutes a criminal offense that endangers civilians and IDF troops," the military said.[1][2]
